overview: This Senate resolution designates May 2026 as "National Brain Tumor Awareness Month." It notes that more than 100,000 people in the U.S. are diagnosed with a primary brain tumor each year, that brain tumors are the leading cause of cancer death in children and teens, and that few new treatments for malignant brain tumors have been approved since the 1980s. The resolution encourages public awareness, supports efforts to develop better treatments, expresses support for patients and their families, and urges researchers to work together. It is symbolic and does not create any program or spending. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 20, 2026.
for: Supporters say raising awareness of brain tumors, which have seen little progress in survival for decades, can build support for research and help patients and families.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or direct new money to brain tumor research.
